chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from some of those who narrated it, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If wine or an intoxicating nabidh touches your garment, then wash it if you know its place; and if you do not know its place, then wash all of it. If you prayed in it, then repeat your salat (prayer).

key_terms.خَمْرٌ: wine; an intoxicating liquid that renders the garment impure in this context
key_terms.صَلَّيْتَ: you prayed; refers to performing salat (prayer) in the garment
key_terms.فَأَعِدْ صَلَاتَكَ: then repeat your salat (prayer); indicating the need to perform the prayer again
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: then wash it; the commanded act of purification
key_terms.مَوْضِعَهُ: its place; the exact spot of contamination on the garment
key_terms.نَبِيذٌ مُسْكِرٌ: intoxicating nabidh; a fermented drink treated here like wine

ai.seo_question: What should be done if wine or intoxicating nabidh gets on one's clothes before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a garment contaminated by wine or intoxicating nabidh. It instructs washing the affected spot when known, or the entire garment when the spot is unknown, and it requires repeating the salat (prayer) if one has prayed in such a garment.
